cohort: Women with a breech-presenting fetus at >33 weeks gestation
finding: The pilot study found that offering OptiBreech collaborative care led to a higher proportion of women planning a vaginal breech birth and resulted in lower rates of cephalic presentation at birth, caesarean birth, neonatal intensive care admission, and severe neonatal morbidity; however, randomisation was deemed unfeasible due to the lack of access to vaginal breech birth within the standard care group.
mod_finding: Women randomised to the OptiBreech care group had higher rates of vaginal birth and lower rates of in-labour caesarean birth compared to the standard care group.
